note: [agent-bulk] The best-formed shower in my shard, and the verdict is a boundary nit, not a failure - please read the magnitude. shw 72066 (268.1 MeV, 15 seg, 56.2 cm, gamma1 of reco pi0 group 0) is textbook on shw72066-az+085-el+20: a narrow stem rising from the X (which sits 13.6 cm off the blue vertex star, where the 56.4 cm muon 4011 and the two pions 4012/4065 of cluster 4 end, all correctly unowned), then a wide broadening cone with a heavy point cloud, then a sparse fading tail - one apex, one direction, on both azimuths. The under-clustering: its acceptance plot shows the pass-1 steps as 30 deg out to 80 cm, 20 deg from 80 to 130 cm, 15 deg beyond, and TWO non-member circles sit INSIDE those boxes - 41027 (0.74 cm, pdg 11) at 84.5 cm / 18.8 deg and 31017 (0.33 cm, pdg 11) at 120.7 cm / 15.3 deg - while the shower does own members at 88.5, 89.5, 103.4 and 111.5 cm at 10-15 deg, i.e. exactly the same population. Both marked IN. That is 1.07 cm of polyline out in the tail; the energy effect is negligible and nothing large is missing. NOT marked: 42028 (1.43 cm, pdg 2212) at 139.3 cm / 11.6 deg, which also falls inside the tier-3 box - a proton 1.4 m out does not belong in this shower and leaving it out is right. Not over-clustered: I checked the same worry I raised on evt292643 (a 268 MeV shower reaching 111 cm) and here the picture answers it - the charge is continuous from the stem through the cone into the tail with no empty gap, so the far members are the tail of one object. Also examined: shw 68035 (41.7 MeV, 4 seg, 10.2 cm, gamma2), a compact core plus two sub-cm stubs at 29.4 and 40.7 cm along its own axis at 3.9 and 8.1 deg; nothing unclaimed in its cone (its nearest non-members 34020 and 36022 are at 53.7 and 36.6 deg), so it reads correct. PI0: this one is clean and worth contrasting with evt292643. The reco paired 72066 + 68035, stored mass 141.5 MeV, and for once the display's two conventions AGREE - axis convention theta 94.5 deg -> 155.2 MeV, vertex convention theta 94.0 deg -> 154.7 MeV, both inside the accept window. pio-az-055-el+020 shows why: both gamma starts are detached from the magenta vertex star and their arrows diverge widely (blue gamma1 to the left, red gamma2 up-right), so there is no small-angle ambiguity for the conventions to disagree about. Scope: 2 showers of 15 examined; 13 skipped by the <20 MeV rule and not looked at. The vtx-* sweep is half-span 129 cm and was used for topology only. Verdict is about clustering and silent on PID.
